desc:
The edit distance between two strings is the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and replacements needed to turn one into the other.

Given s, t and a small integer k, return the edit distance between s and t if it is at most k, and -1 otherwise. The strings can be thousands of characters long, so a full m × n table is too slow; use the fact that k is small.

s = "kitten", t = "sitting", k = 3  ->  3
s = "kitten", t = "sitting", k = 2  -> -1
s = "abc",    t = "abc",     k = 0  ->  0
s = "abcd",   t = "abcdefgh", k = 3  -> -1   (the length gap alone is 4)
constraints: Both strings contain only lowercase English letters
hints: A full table has up to 36 million cells. Which cells can ever be part of a path of cost at most k?
A cell (i, j) needs at least |i - j| insertions or deletions just to get there, so only cells with |i - j| ≤ k matter: a band of width 2k+1 around the diagonal.

Store only the band: index each row by d = j - i + k in [0, 2k]. The diagonal move keeps d, a delete reads d+1 of the previous row, an insert reads d-1 of the current row. Treat everything outside the band as 'more than k'.
editorial: Any alignment that reaches table cell (i, j) has already used at least |i - j| insertions or deletions, because every unit of difference between the two prefix lengths needs one. A path of total cost at most k therefore never leaves the band |i - j| ≤ k. Cells outside the band can be treated as infinity, so only 2k + 1 cells per row need computing. If |len(s) - len(t)| > k the answer is immediately -1.

Index row i by the offset d = j - i + k. The cell above-left (a match or replacement) has the same offset in the previous row, the cell above (a delete) is offset d + 1 in the previous row, and the cell to the left (an insert) is offset d - 1 in the same row. Clamp values at k + 1 to keep numbers small. The final answer is the value at the bottom-right cell if it is at most k. Total time is O(n · k) instead of O(m · n), which for 6,000 characters and k = 20 is about 250,000 cells instead of 36 million.
